Independent exact replay for p=31,43: enumerate f(u) and all fibers. For g=3 and χ_j(g)=exp(2πij/m), reduce Σ_{i=0}^{m−1} X^{(pji+mf(g^i)) mod(pm)} modulo Φ_pm over the integers. The zero-remainder indices were {10,20} at 31 and {7,14,28,35} at 43, giving ranks 28 and 38 with t=10 and 7. The fibers over 1 were {6,16,26} and {7,22,37}; all fibers had size three.
correctness.rationale: The proof establishes the exact complex rank and right kernel, not just a lower bound on the defect. With m=p−1, take d to be the specified nonzero representative of −k−1 modulo m. The product phase is f(u)=u(1+u^k), so a right character vector maps to the inverse character times its scalar phase sum. Here k is even, k≡1 mod 3, and gcd(k,m)=m/3. The index-three subgroup H=ker(u↦u^k) contains −1 and 2; 3 does not divide |H|. On the three cosets H, ωH, ω²H the multipliers of f are respectively 2, −ω² and −ω. Each is a bijection from its coset onto H, giving exactly {h/2,−ωh,−ω²h} over each h. Factoring these fibers gives the stated bracket and the common period. The period cannot vanish: adjoining ζ_p to Q(ζ_m) gives Q(ζ_pm), of relative degree p−1 by coprimality; its only possible degree-at-most-p−1 polynomial relation is a multiple of Φ_p, but the period polynomial has zero constant term and nonzero coefficients on H. Thus the bracket vanishes exactly for χ(−2)=1 and χ(ω)≠1. Subtracting the annihilator of ⟨−2,ω⟩, of size m/(3t), from that of ⟨−2⟩, of size m/t, proves the count. This also justifies subtracting exactly that many dimensions from m: character inversion permutes a basis.
residual_risks: The independent finite checks certify these two examples only. The analytic argument covers all primes under the two stated arithmetic hypotheses. No extension-field, infinitude or conditioning claim is certified.

evidence: The binomial theorems bound parameters of permutation binomials and describe equivalence to binomials over subfields; the phase here is not a permutation. Even a nonpermutation criterion does not give the character sums on its fibers.

Forey–Fresán–Kowalski's introductory generic and stratified vanishing concerns perverse-sheaf cohomology of twists over finite field extensions, with estimates for exceptional sets. The inspected statement is not an exact character-by-character cancellation theorem for this phase.

Tao's nonvanishing-minor formulation applies to the one-dimensional prime cyclic Fourier matrix. The matrix in the finding is a restriction in additive dimension two; its entries depend on a binomial of the product and are not the one-dimensional minor setting.
broader_coverage.reasoning: None of these broader statements gives the exact exceptional characters by specializing an applicable general formula. The distinction is the weighted fibers, not just whether the binomial is injective.

value.rationale: Square sampling on a single algebraic curve need not permit recovery even at equal numbers of sites and samples. The index-three resonance is motivated by all the phase cosets mapping onto one subgroup, rather than by selecting examples with numerical rank drops. The result quantifies how much information is lost, using an order rather than only the image size, and identifies every unrecoverable character. This is an exact structural invariant for the full stated family; it distinguishes higher-dimensional loss from the inverse-hyperbola obstruction.
residual_risks: Value is localized to this family: the result gives neither a rank classification for arbitrary exponents nor recovery stability for the nonzero modes.
